text: The aging process is associated with alterations in both the quantity and quality of muscle. Human muscle mass reaches peak levels between the ages of 20 and 40 (14). Thereafter, the body loses approximately 0.5% of its muscle mass per year during the fourth decade of life, increasing to 1% to 2% annually after the age of 50 and then accelerating to 3% annually after the age of 60 () (91, 97). This age-related loss of muscle tissue has been termed sarcopenia . Sedentary people show larger rates of decline than those who are active, although leisure time physical activity has only minor effects on tempering muscle loss (91).
